Select the Hyperparameters of a Kinked Penalty Along a Path

Source: R/path.R
statmod_path.Rd

Sweeps the hyperparameters of the kinked penalties over grids of kink sizes and keeps the setting at which the criterion is best, by its minimum or by the one-standard-error rule.

Usage

statmod_path(
  spec,
  design,
  blocks,
  hyper,
  inner_optimizer,
  method,
  optimizer,
  beta,
  emethod,
  maxit,
  tol,
  vb,
  data,
  rows,
  sweeps = 2L,
  nested_method = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design.

blocks

The blocks.

hyper

The hyperparameters.

inner_optimizer

The inner method.

method

The OuterMethod() that scores the points of the path.

optimizer

The optimizer for the differentiable hyperparameters.

beta

The starting coefficients.

emethod

The method that obtains the expected information: NULL (the closed form of the family where it has one, and distributions7::expect_opg() otherwise) or an object that inherits from distributions7::ExpectMethod. It is read only where the expected information is used.

maxit, tol

The inner budget.

vb

The verbosity.

data

The data with which the fit was called, which cross-validation needs in order to refit on part of it; the weights and offsets are those held by spec.

rows

The axes to select, as path_rows() returns them.

sweeps

The largest number of cyclic passes, 2 by default.

nested_method

The OuterMethod() that estimates the differentiable hyperparameters inside each point of the path, or NULL, in which case method is used.

Value

A list with par, hyper, value, criterion, converged, obj, hist_blocks, hist_inner, hist_outer, iterations, evaluations, exact_gradient and exact_hessian: the fields of outer_fit()'s result that a path produces. criterion is the value of method at the setting chosen, and hist_outer has one row for each point visited.

Details

The grid runs from the kink that empties the block down to min_ratio of it, so the sweep goes from the sparsest fit towards the fullest and every fit starts from the previous one's coefficients. The top of the grid is computed at the coefficients in hand and not at a refitted null; where the fit at the top does not empty the block, the top is doubled until it does.

For a term that carries several of these hyperparameters, every combination is visited where the term sets search = "grid" and one coordinate at a time where it sets "cyclic". Between terms the alternation is cyclic either way, so that the cost is the product within a term and the sum across terms. Each axis is built at the settings of the axes outside it, which makes the elastic net's grid a family of \(\lambda\) axes and not a single one, and the axis swept by kink size is put innermost so that the warm starts walk along it. The runs of a product grid are independent and are distributed over worker processes where the specification requests them.

A pass that would visit the points scored by the previous one is not run. The top of the path is computed again at every pass, because the rest of the model moves, and where it has not moved the grid is the one already in hand. The function makes at most sweeps passes, and only where more than one hyperparameter is selected.

Where the model also carries hyperparameters that are twice differentiable, those are estimated by outer_fit() inside each point of the path, by nested_method, so that the two kinds are not mixed into one search. The unpenalized coefficients of a dispersion are then held at the joint mode along the path when nested_method is a marginal criterion, and are estimated on that criterion once, at the setting chosen.

An error is signaled where method is aic(), bic() or cv() and the path scores no point. A warning is signaled where the rule is "min", the axis is swept by kink size, and the minimum lies at the dense end of the path and the criterion is still falling there.
